decisive_items: extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma of the left foot treated 9 years earlier
Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mass arising from the right frontal diploic space
Noncontrast head CT revealed a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone with hypodense soft‐tissue extension into the scalp
response.rationale: Known extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma with a new lytic frontal diploic mass and scalp/intracranial extension is most consistent with metastatic disease; primary skull tumors and lipoma are less supported.

rejected.why: Same metastatic diagnosis but lacks frontal bone specificity; less precise than R1C.
Primary osteosarcoma would not explain prior ESMC history and lacks osteoid matrix features.
Giant cell tumor typically involves sphenoid/temporal and lacks prior sarcoma link.
Chordoma is clival/sacral, not frontal diploic.
Plasmacytoma possible but less likely given known ESMC history; no systemic myeloma features.
Lipoma was initial thought; imaging shows intraosseous lytic lesion, not superficial lipoma.
Too nonspecific; bone tumor is descriptive, not a specific diagnosis.
Descriptive lytic bone tumor; lacks metastatic ESMC etiology.
Soft tissue sarcoma is broad and ignores intraosseous origin/history.
Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma alone ignores metastatic spread to bone.
Trauma was remote and lesion enlarged; imaging shows destructive bone lesion, not simple traumatic lesion.
Primary skull chondrosarcoma is less likely than metastasis from known ESMC.
No radiation history to skull; prior chemotherapy not radiation.
